subject: physiology
title: GIP, Motilin, Somatostatin, and Enterogastrone Actions

steps.tx: The discovery that orally administered glucose stimulates significantly greater insulin secretion than an identical amount infused intravenously established the existence of the **incretin effect**. Intestinal endocrine cells sense luminal carbohydrates and fats, releasing peptide hormones that prime pancreatic beta cells in advance of nutrient absorption.
steps.say: The incretin effect explains why oral glucose triggers much more insulin release than intravenous glucose.

left.title: Oral Glucose Challenge
points: Nutrients contact enteroendocrine K and L cells in gut
Stimulates massive release of GIP and GLP-1 into portal blood
Incretins prime pancreatic beta cells via cyclic AMP
Accounts for 50% to 70% of total postprandial insulin release

right.title: Intravenous Glucose Infusion
points: Zero stimulation of intestinal K and L cells (no incretin surge)
Beta cells stimulated solely by arterial hyperglycaemia
Produces modest, delayed insulin release with higher peak glycaemia

steps.tx: Synthesized and secreted by enteroendocrine K cells concentrated in the duodenum and jejunum, **glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide**, or GIP, is released in response to luminal glucose and amino acids. GIP binds beta-cell receptors to elevate cyclic AMP, stimulating glucose-dependent exocytosis of insulin.
steps.say: GIP is secreted by duodenal K cells in response to glucose, stimulating insulin release in a glucose-dependent manner.

nodes.label: Duodenal K Cells Sense Luminal Glucose and Fatty Acids
GIP Secreted into Portal Circulation and Traverses to Islets of Langerhans
Binds GIP Receptor on Pancreatic Beta Cells -> Elevates Intracellular cAMP
Potentiates Exocytosis of Insulin Storage Granules Strictly During Hyperglycaemia

steps.tx: The hormone signal from a meal is erased within minutes by one enzyme. **Dipeptidyl peptidase-4** clips and inactivates GIP and GLP-1, ending their insulin releasing message almost as soon as it begins. Blocking that enzyme with gliptin drugs stretches the incretin signal through a meal without forcing insulin out when glucose is low. That glucose dependence is why this class rarely causes hypoglycaemia on its own.
steps.say: DPP-4 rapidly inactivates incretin hormones GIP and GLP-1. Blocking it prolongs their glucose dependent insulin signal.

vis.alt: Image showing dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inactivating incretin hormones.
vis.caption: An enzyme is shown clipping an incretin molecule into inactive fragments. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Co-secreted from distal ileal and colonic L cells, glucagon-like peptide 1 exerts synergistic incretin actions while suppressing glucagon and slowing gastric emptying. Both circulating incretins undergo rapid enzymatic degradation within minutes by **dipeptidyl peptidase-4**, providing a primary pharmaceutical target for oral gliptin antidiabetic therapies.
steps.say: Incretins are rapidly degraded by dipeptidyl peptidase-4, making DPP-4 inhibitors effective oral therapies for type 2 diabetes.

steps.tx: Synthesized by enterochromaffin-like M cells in the duodenal and jejunal mucosa, the cyclic peptide **motilin** functions as the master regulator of fasting gastrointestinal motor patterns. Released in periodic twenty-minute pulses during the interdigestive state, motilin initiates Phase III of the migrating motor complex.
steps.say: Motilin is secreted by duodenal M cells during fasting, triggering migrating motor complex waves every ninety minutes.

nodes.label: Interdigestive Fasting State: Absence of Luminal Nutrients in Upper Gut
Duodenal M Cells Release Periodic Cyclical Surges of Peptide Motilin
Initiates Phase III Migrating Motor Complex (MMC) in Gastric Antrum
High-Amplitude Housekeeping Peristalsis Propels Undigested Debris into Colon

steps.tx: Erythromycin and related macrolide antibiotics act as direct pharmacological agonists at **motilin receptors**, stimulating robust gastrointestinal contractions. Clinically, erythromycin is utilized off-label as a prokinetic agent to accelerate gastric emptying in diabetic gastroparesis and clear the gastric fundus prior to emergency endoscopy.
steps.say: Macrolide antibiotics like erythromycin bind motilin receptors, serving as powerful prokinetic agents in gastroparesis.

left.title: Endogenous Motilin
points: 22-amino-acid peptide secreted by mucosal M cells
Suppressed immediately upon ingestion of meals
Coordinates cyclical Phase III contractions every 90 to 120 minutes

right.title: Macrolide Prokinetics (Erythromycin)
points: Direct non-peptide agonist at human motilin receptors
Accelerates stomach emptying in diabetic gastroparesis
Tachyphylaxis develops within days due to receptor downregulation

steps.tx: Emergency endoscopy of bleeding esophageal varices fails if the fundus is still full of blood and food. Erythromycin and related macrolide antibiotics are direct agonists at **motilin receptors** and provoke strong gastrointestinal contractions. Used off label as a prokinetic, erythromycin speeds gastric emptying in diabetic gastroparesis and is given to clear the gastric fundus before an urgent endoscopy. The same contractions that empty a paretic stomach therefore uncover the variceal columns the scope has to treat.
steps.say: Erythromycin binds motilin receptors and triggers forceful gut contractions. Off label, that prokinetic effect empties the stomach in diabetic gastroparesis and clears the fundus before emergency endoscopy, so varices are not hidden by retained blood and food.

vis.alt: An endoscopic view shows dilated tortuous veins bulging into the lower esophageal lumen.
vis.caption: Columns of esophageal varices crowd the distal lumen as they would appear when an emergency endoscope reaches the lower esophagus. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Functioning as the universal gastrointestinal brake, the peptide **somatostatin** is synthesized by D cells dispersed throughout the gastric mucosa, pancreatic islets, and enteric plexuses. Secreted in both paracrine and endocrine modes, somatostatin exerts widespread inhibitory actions across all digestive secretory and motor processes.
steps.say: Somatostatin is the universal inhibitory brake of the gut, shutting down acid, enzymes, insulin, and blood flow.

rows: Suppresses gastrin release when luminal pH < 3.0
Directly inhibits histamine release and acid secretion
Pancreatic Islet Beta and Alpha Cells
Inhibits both insulin and glucagon secretion
Produces marked splanchnic vasoconstriction (reduces portal pressure)
Inhibits fluid and electrolyte secretion, slowing motility

steps.tx: Long-acting synthetic somatostatin analogues like octreotide provide indispensable pharmacotherapy across diverse endocrine and gastroenterological emergencies. By constricting splanchnic arterioles, octreotide blunts portal blood inflow to arrest acute bleeding from **esophageal varices**, while suppressing secretory diarrhea in neuroendocrine carcinoid syndrome and VIP-secreting tumors.
steps.say: Octreotide mimics somatostatin, reducing portal blood flow to halt bleeding varices and controlling carcinoid syndrome.

vis.caption: Somatostatin D-cell paracrine networks, proton suppression, and splanchnic haemodynamic control.

steps.tx: Collectively, hormonal factors that inhibit gastric acid secretion and motility upon arrival of chyme in the small intestine are known as **enterogastrones**. Encompassing secretin, cholecystokinin, GIP, and peptide YY, enterogastrones safeguard the duodenal mucosa from acid injury and match gastric emptying to duodenal absorptive capacity.
steps.say: Enterogastrones include secretin, CCK, and GIP, coordinating duodenal feedback to slow gastric emptying and acid output.
